candidate.blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — identify risk factors and prevent complications
candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — pressure-injury risk assessment
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize major patient factors that increase pressure-injury risk.

options.A: Full mobility, intact sensation, adequate nutrition, and dry skin.
options.B: Independent repositioning, intact sensation, and adequate nutritional intake.
options.C: Frequent ambulation, intact sensory perception, and no moisture exposure.
options.D: Limited mobility, impaired sensory perception, poor nutrition, and persistent moisture exposure.

candidate.rationale: Current NCBI guidance identifies decreased mobility, moisture, poor nutritional status, and loss of sensory perception among the major pressure-injury risk factors. These same domains are included in the Braden risk assessment framework. D is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Common pressure-injury risk factors include decreased mobility, moisture, poor nutritional status, and loss of sensory perception; Braden assesses sensory perception, moisture, activity, mobility, nutrition, and friction/shear.
candidate.source_locator: Etiology; History and Physical; Evaluation — Braden Scale
candidate.source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), StatPearls
candidate.stem: Which combination of findings places a hospitalized client at increased risk for pressure injury?
